_comment: mwcceppc (GameCube PowerPC) codegen lever catalogue. One lever per line; read it with tools/levers.py, not by hand-parsing. This is a DISTILLED INDEX, not the evidence - `source` points at where each was actually derived. Schema is deliberately identical to tangosdev/sm64ds-decomp notes/levers.jsonl so the two are readable by the same tool across a sibling checkout; that catalogue covers mwccarm/NDS and this one covers mwcceppc/GameCube. Fields: arch = ISAs the mechanism is known or believed to work on; compiler_version = the mwcceppc versions it was established on, because GC/1.x and GC/2.x+ differ materially; confidence = proven (reproduced a byte-match) or probable.

symptom: every instruction matches but the whole function is shifted: stwu r1,-N(r1) reserves less than the target and every stack displacement is off by a constant
lever: the original produced more intermediate values here. GC/1.x never reclaims a stack slot, so anything that failed to win a register still costs frame even when its code was optimized away entirely. Find the inline call or longer expression chain that creates the missing temporaries; do NOT paper over it with a dummy local, that is a fakematch
note: the mwccarm catalogue's `volatile-local-stack-slot` is the sibling of this, but the mechanism differs: mwccarm DOES reclaim and needs volatile to pin a slot, whereas GC/1.x never reclaims at all. MEASURED REFINEMENT: frames carry 4 bytes of alignment padding, so one added 4-byte temporary is absorbed and does not move the frame at all. A +8 delta therefore means TWO more intermediate values, not one - do not go looking for a single missing local
tooling: tools/stack-frame-diff.py finds every instance tree-wide; mwcc-izer `stack -w` says what occupies one frame and which inlined call put it there
source: sms:tools/stack-frame-diff.py, proven on control__14TMapObjGeneralFv and THPPlayerInit
diagnosis: run mwcc-izer `stack -w` on the function and on a SIBLING that already matches, then compare the `by kind` line. Frames decompose into linkage / arguments / temps / saved registers / padding, and the deficit is in exactly one of those. Rule out the cheap explanations first: (a) extra callee-saved registers cannot be it if the function is frame-only, because saving another register adds stw/lwz instructions and would change the length - check the prologue bytes directly; (b) by-value class parameters do not home to the stack on mwcceppc, unlike mwccarm. What is left is compiler temporaries, one per intermediate value, which are created by inlined calls
worked_example: the receiveMessage(THitActor*,u32) cluster: 9 overrides across 8 files sit at 0x20 and want 0x28, with byte-identical frame composition (arg 12 / linkage 8 / temp 4 / padding 4 / saved 4). Verified from the raw prologues that target and ours both save only r31 and are the same length, so the target's extra 8 bytes are two more temporaries that generate no code. Still unsolved; whoever cracks one likely gets all nine

symptom: a call is a bl in your build where the target inlined it, or the reverse; or the linker map wants a weak out-of-line copy of an inline function that you never emit
lever: MWCC gates inlining on STATEMENT COUNT, not code size. CInline_IsSmallFunction refuses anything over 15 statements outright. Past that the budget is per nesting pass: pass 0 (written directly in the function's own source) unlimited, pass 1 limit 10, pass 2 limit 7, pass 3 limit 3, pass 4 never runs. A call appearing as an ARGUMENT to another call counts one pass deeper. To make MWCC emit a weak out-of-line copy, arrange for at least one call to FAIL to inline
note: definition order does NOT gate inlining on GC/1.2.5 - a callee defined later still inlines. The widely repeated 'define before use' rule is false for this compiler
tooling: mwcc-izer inline_trace.py reports the compiler's own accept/refuse reason and every callee's statement count
source: sms: getCurBckAnmPtr emitted at the map's exact size by collapsing setBckAnm from 15 to <=10 statements

symptom: a helper inlines at its top-level call site but stays a bl one layer deeper, truncating an inline chain you need
lever: collapse statements to get the function under the budget for the pass it is called at - an if/else folded into a ternary, or a declaration merged with its initialiser, each remove a statement. 15 is the hard gate; 10 is what matters at pass 1

symptom: __vt__ for a class lands in the wrong translation unit, taking its weak inline-virtual bodies and @NN@ adjustor thunks with it
lever: MWCC emits the vtable in the TU that defines the class's first non-inline, non-pure virtual in DECLARATION order. Move that declaration to change which TU owns the vtable. Reordering an OVERRIDE is layout-safe because the base fixes the slot; the destructor is also safe to move, MWCC pins it to its own slot
source: sms:include/MoveBG/MapObjGeneral.hpp, initMapObj promoted to first virtual

symptom: functions are all present and matching but sit in the wrong order in .text relative to the linker map
lever: with -inline deferred, .text emission order is the REVERSE of definition order in the source. Reorder the definitions, not the declarations
tooling: tools/validate-symbol-order.py (reverse_fn_order: True); tools/check-changed-symbol-order.py gates it in CI

symptom: you have declared a member virtual, but the linker map lists that symbol as UNUSED
lever: that combination is impossible: a virtual's address lives in a vtable, so mwld can never prove it unreachable and can never strip it. If the map says UNUSED, the original was not virtual - fix the declaration
note: checked across 2883 virtual declarations against 5134 UNUSED entries in mario.MAP: zero conflicts, so the invariant holds and is cheap to assert in CI

symptom: the function is byte-identical except that some values were coloured into different registers - same opcodes, same immediates, same structure
lever: recognise it and move on. MWCC's allocator is non-local: the colour a temp gets depends on whole-function register pressure, not the local statement, so there is no source construct that reliably forces a specific register. Changing the SHAPE of the computation (adding or removing a temporary) nudges pressure and is the only lever, but it is a shove not a dial
note: cross-checked against tangosdev/sm64ds-decomp, which reports the same wall on mwccarm and calls it the dominant blocker there. On SMS it is rare - only 20 of 2190 failing functions are pure register permutation - so unlike the ARM title this is NOT where our remaining work sits
tooling: tools/stack-frame-diff.py reports a `regperm` bucket; mwcc-izer dumps the allocator's priority list and coalescing state, which is the only way to see why a colour was chosen
source: sms: 20 cases measured 2026-08-22; mechanism per the mwcc-debugger README (github.com/cadmic/mwcc-debugger) and sm64ds notes/mwccarm-codegen.md section 2
